findings.claim: Q2 mark scheme: 'Do not accept con sordino (this is a brass technique).'
findings.truth: Con sordino is not brass-only. String players mute by clipping a mute to the bridge, and con sordino is standard string notation. The stated reason for rejecting it is false and would teach a wrong fact.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mute_(music) (string mutes fit on the bridge; con sordino is a string and brass direction)

findings.claim: con sordino: 'A brass technique where a mute is placed inside the bell of the instrument...'
findings.truth: Con sordino means 'with mute' for strings and brass alike. Corrected in the glossary and in the matching data-def in the body.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mute_(music)

findings.claim: Jaws: 'The tremolo and accented notes on the strings create growing tension and fear.' The Q3 scheme also credits 'Tremolo creates a shimmering, anxious effect'.
findings.truth: The shark motif is a repeated accented rising semitone (E to F) in the low register, played by tuba and low strings. Tremolo is not a feature of it.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaws_(soundtrack)

findings.claim: Toto, Africa: 'The intro is in A major with chords I-vii-iii, while the verse modulates to B major... The chorus uses a vi-IV-I-V progression.'
findings.truth: The keys are the wrong way round. The board's published analysis of this set extract puts the four-bar intro in B major (chords flat-VII, vi, ii = A, G#m, C#m) and Verse 1 in B major; it is the chorus that moves to A major, where vi-IV-I-V is F#m-D-A-E. (The appendix allows B major, E major or A lydian for the intro - A major is not one of them.)
findings.evidence: https://resource.download.wjec.co.uk/vtc/2019-20/WJEC19-20_1-10/pdf/eduqas-toto-africa-musical-analysis-update-10-20.pdf pp.1-3 and appendix p.7

findings.truth: Fusion is named only in the Popular Music area of study. A film score that blends traditions is still fair AoS3 listening material (the AoS3 list covers timbre, tone colour and instrumental colour/mood), so the case studies stand. The open question is whether Tom wants the lesson re-badged as a cross-area lesson, or the bhangra and Africa sections moved to an AoS4 unit. The edits above remove the false spec claims but keep the lesson where it is.

summary: Five lessons, 31 findings. Seven places named the exam board to students and four mark schemes claimed written-communication marks that this qualification does not award. Lesson 5 taught bhangra and fusion as Film Music when the spec sets them under Popular Music, labelled a Film Music question as a prepared extract with score (Film Music has no set work), and reversed the keys of the Toto Africa intro, verse and chorus. Thirteen practice questions carried a marks label that contradicted their own scheme, three decks held mangled cloze flashcards, and lesson 3 told students con sordino is brass-only.
